units.title: Component 1: Voices in Speech and Writing

outcomes.text: Explain how spoken voices are formed and written voices created in literary, non-literary and digital texts.
Explain how writers and speakers shape language to present an identity or persona.
Apply methods of text analysis from both linguistic and literary fields.
Choose reading and listening strategies to suit text type and purpose.
Describe how meanings and effects are created, using language levels: phonetics, lexis, grammar, pragmatics, discourse.
Explain how texts relate to the contexts of their production and reception.
Explore connections across literary and non-literary texts.
Evaluate a text's effectiveness for different audiences and purposes.
Study non-literary and digital 20th- and 21st-century texts such as interviews, podcasts, blogs, screenplays and travelogues.
Analyse linguistic and literary features and generic conventions of non-literary and digital forms.
Study one set drama text, such as A Streetcar Named Desire or The History Boys, to see how writers create voices.

units.title: Component 2: Varieties in Language and Literature

outcomes.text: Analyse how writers use language techniques and literary devices to convey ideas on a theme.
Explore how different writers convey similar themes and issues in different texts.
Explain how different readers or listeners interpret individual texts.
Read widely across non-fiction genres to respond to an unseen prose non-fiction extract.
Study an anchor novel such as The Great Gatsby or Great Expectations with a second text on this theme.
Study an anchor novel such as A Single Man or Tess of the D'Urbervilles with a second text on this theme.
Study an anchor novel such as A Room with a View or Wuthering Heights with a second text on this theme.
Study an anchor novel such as Wide Sargasso Sea or Dracula with a second text on this theme.
Compare a prose fiction anchor text with a second prose, drama or poetry text from the same theme.
